message.$description: The fourth piece of the Message/Bubble/Attachment family (see the approved plan) and the actual centerpiece of the original ask — the rich, institution-authored content block (headings-as-bold-labels, mixed text, bulleted links, images, one or more file Attachments, one CTA button). Chrome default is NONE — a plain block, sender row (Avatar + name + timestamp, one line, matching the real live desktop Message Center app exactly) above a body, no bubble shape, no border, no fill. This is a deliberate choice over the staff-mobile mockups' white-bubble chrome for the same content: the live product is the source of truth, the mockup's chrome is documented as an optional 'card' variant below, not built as the default. Deliberately NOT the same component as Bubble (the plain-text-only reply sibling, not yet built) — content-type split, not sender-based, confirmed against the actual screenshots: even a staff member's own short reply renders as a Bubble, and this rich block is reserved for genuinely formatted content. Sizing/typography mostly reuses existing pieces wholesale (Avatar, Button for the CTA, text-style.body-base/link-base) rather than recomposing them — only the layout rhythm (gaps) and two small pieces (sender-row typography, list spacing) are new.

sender.$description: Avatar + a single text line ('Name -- Dec 19, 2:54 PM') — not two stacked lines. 2026-07-24 rebalance per explicit feedback: the avatar is the SM size (32px, resolved from avatar.tokens.json), not base — a 40px avatar next to one small text line read top-heavy — and the name is text.secondary, not text.default, so the sender line stops competing with the body for attention (the timestamp stays text.muted, one step quieter still).

body.$description: Paragraph text reuses text-style.body-base verbatim (not recomposed). A 'subheading' ('Important Details') and an inline run-in label ('Dates:') are the SAME treatment — weight.semibold on body-base's own size — applied either to a standalone paragraph or to a <strong> at the start of one; no second typography composite needed for what's visually one bold-emphasis idea used two ways.

attachments.$description: One or more real, unmodified Attachments (resolved from attachment.tokens.json, not retyped) can sit in the body flow — e.g. a financial-aid notice with an attached form. No new token: they space using the same body.gap as every other body element, and stack with their own dim.1_5 gap when there's more than one, matching Attachment's own internal rhythm rather than inventing a second one.

cta.$description: A CTA button is a real component.button (primary, base size), reused as-is — only the spacing before it is this component's own token.

card.$description: Optional chrome — reuses Card's own exact recipe (surface.default + border.default + radius.default + dim.4 padding) rather than inventing a lookalike. The component default remains chromeless, but the Message Center thread view DOES use this variant per explicit 2026-07-24 feedback (a chromeless institution message floating on the page read oddly there) — partially reversing the earlier 'live product outranks mockup' call for that one surface.
